plugin.name: Reverse Proxy
plugin.description: Reverse proxy for TCP, UDP, HTTP and HTTPS with free certificates and Termix login, managed per host.

tab.title: Reverse Proxy
tab.error: Could not load the reverse proxy.
tab.needsBaseUrl: Some routes ask for Termix login, but the Termix address is not set. Set it in the Reverse Proxy settings or those routes cannot open.
tab.noHost: Open the reverse proxy from a host.
tab.hostOff: Reverse proxy is turned off for this host in its settings. Existing routes are paused.

form.name: Name
form.domainHint: Point this domain's DNS at this server. A wildcard like *.example.com works for routing.
form.publicPortHint: The port this server listens on. Publish it in your Docker setup too.
form.targetAddressHint: Leave empty to use this host's own address.

certHint.acme: A free certificate is requested and renewed for you. Port 80 must reach the HTTP port of this plugin.
certHint.selfsigned: Browsers will warn about it. Fine for private use.
certHint.custom: Add your certificate on the Certificates view first.

form.forceHttpsDesc: Visitors on plain HTTP are sent to the secure address.
form.accessHost: Users with access to this host

accessHint.none: No login in front of this route.
accessHint.user: Visitors sign in with Termix first.
accessHint.host: Visitors sign in with Termix and must be able to connect to this host.

form.targetHttpsDesc: Connect to the target with TLS.
form.insecureTargetDesc: Skip certificate checks on the target. Use for self-signed services.
form.preserveHostDesc: Send the visitor's domain to the target instead of the target address.
form.httpsPublicPortHint: Only if visitors reach HTTPS on a port other than 443. Used for the redirect. 0 means 443.
form.headersHint: One per line as Name: value. Sent to the target.
form.allowIpsHint: IPs or ranges, one per line. Empty allows everyone.
form.idleSecondsHint: Close a quiet connection after this long. 0 uses the default.

list.empty: No routes match. Add one with the Add route button.
list.deleteDesc: The route stops right away. Certificates stay.

certs.autoNote: Let's Encrypt certificates are requested when you add a route and renew on their own.
certs.needsEmail: Set an email for Let's Encrypt in the Reverse Proxy settings before using automatic certificates.
certs.domainsHint: One or more domains, separated by spaces or commas.
certs.deleteDesc: Routes that use it must be changed first.

use.title: Manage reverse proxy routes
use.description: Open the Reverse Proxy tab and add routes to hosts you can edit.

access.title: Open protected routes
access.description: Sign in to web routes that ask for a Termix login.

httpPort.label: HTTP port
httpPort.description: The port this plugin listens on for HTTP. Map your public port 80 to it. Needed for Let's Encrypt.

httpsPort.label: HTTPS port
httpsPort.description: The port this plugin listens on for HTTPS. Map your public port 443 to it.

bindHost.label: Listen address
bindHost.description: Use 0.0.0.0 to accept connections from anywhere, or 127.0.0.1 to keep routes local.

publicBaseUrl.label: Termix address
publicBaseUrl.description: The address people use to open Termix, like https://termix.example.com. Needed for routes that ask for Termix login.

acmeEmail.label: Certificate email
acmeEmail.description: Let's Encrypt uses it for expiry notices.

acmeStaging.label: Use Let's Encrypt staging
acmeStaging.description: Test certificates that browsers do not trust. Use while setting up to avoid rate limits.

cookieHours.label: Login length in hours
cookieHours.description: How long a visitor stays signed in on a protected route.

acmeDirectoryUrl.label: Custom certificate authority
acmeDirectoryUrl.description: The ACME directory address of another CA, like a private step-ca. Leave empty to use Let's Encrypt.

enable.label: Allow reverse proxy routes
enable.description: Routes for this host are managed in the Reverse Proxy tab. Turn this off to stop them.

targetAddress.label: Target address
targetAddress.description: Where routes send traffic. Leave empty to use this host's own address. Set it to reach a container or another machine.

defaultAccess.label: Default login for new web routes
defaultAccess.description: What new web routes on this host start with.
defaultAccess.host: Users with access to this host
